/THURSDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Issued at 131 PM MDT Tue Oct 20 2026

Thursday...The beginning of an unsettled and wetter pattern will 
commence as the initial negatively tilted shortwave trough aloft, 
emanating from the parent upper trough over southern Nevada, moves 
northeast across our counties during the daylight hours. Dynamics 
associated with this perturbation aloft and orographic effects will 
produce scattered showers in the afternoon across Carbon County, 
including our Snowy and Sierra Madre Ranges. A lull in shower 
coverage is expected Thursday night as the southeast Wyoming is 
somewhat dry slotted. Brisk southerly low level winds will persist 
Thursday night, along with cloud cover to keep minimum temperatures 
rather mild.

Friday...The parent shortwave trough aloft, negatively tilted, moves 
from northern Utah near dawn, to northeast Wyoming by suppertime, 
with the majority of our forecast locations being dry slotted, as 
the bulk of the shortwave trough moisture and lift will be over 
western Wyoming and central Montana. Although, with the approach of 
the Pacific origin cold front and frontal lifting, as well as some 
mid level moisture, you can anticipate, scattered afternoon showers 
for areas bounded roughly by Laramie, Wheatland, Torrington and 
Cheyenne, with the showers moving and/or developing into far eastern 
Wyoming and the Nebraska Panhandle in the evening, before showers 
mainly dissipate late as the rather potent Pacific origin cold front 
sweeps eastward across southeast Wyoming and western Nebraska, with 
orographically driven showers falling across the Northern Laramie, 
Snowy and Sierra Madre Ranges. 

Saturday...A windy and colder day is in tap in the decent thickness 
packing behind the Pacific origin cold front, with winds decreasing 
in the afternoon as pressure gradients slacken off. The next closed 
low aloft moves near the Four Corners by early evening, and with 
orographics combined with diffluence aloft and adequate low and mid 
level moisture, you can expect scattered afternoon showers from the 
Sierra Madre Range eastward across the Snowy Range and across the 
Laramie Valley including Laramie, and to the southern Laramie Range. 
Dry elsewhere, though with cloud cover.

Sunday...Confidence in model solutions is rather low to moderate, at 
this juncture, as an initial spoke of shortwave trough energy is 
progged to move north and northeast across our counties, possibly 
producing scattered to numerous showers dynamically driven, with 
cold air damming near the low levels producing low level mechanical 
lift over and east of the Laramie Range. FOr now, we will blend with 
our neighboring offices early in the day, keeping POPS relatively 
low and mainly southeast of a Laramie to Alliance line. Although 
model trends will need to be watched closely for a possible 
rain/snow scenario early in the day. A cool, overcast afternoon 
looks quite plausible as the shortwave trough aloft opens up over 
central Wyoming with cold surface air upslope remaining underneath 
the southwest flow aloft, which may make for a colder day, than 
currently forecasted, as model trends come into better agreement.

Monday...A decent shortwave trough aloft, positively tilted, moves 
across the Dakotas, with cold surface high pressure remaining dammed 
up along and east of the Interstate 25 corridor and the Laramie 
Range. Confidence in precipitation forecast is minimal in this 
progressive pattern, although with forecast experience, believe 
there is a distinct possibility for colder temperatures than 
currently forecasted if current model trends continue.

Tuesday...Day seven shows the typical model discrepancies in this 
progressive synoptic pattern, leading to a fairly low to moderate 
confidence forecast. Likely a dry scenario with cold northerly flow 
at mid and upper levels and relatively low precipitable water 
values. Again, with 700 mb temperatures progged near -1 Celsius, if 
true, our maximum temperatures will need to be lowered eventually as 
models come into better congruency.
